findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: `mechanisms[]` is the only card class exempt from source, date and confidence — and it is the card the notebook calls the video
findings.expected: A mechanism that IS a rule (an accounting treatment) can name the standard, the paragraph, the year and the filer it binds, and carry that provenance on the card a reviewer sees.
findings.got: `mechanisms[]` is `{id, name, chain[], explains, needs_analogy, note?}` — no source, no as_of, no confidence — while `facts[]` carries all three under a rule reading 'Every fact dated and sourced. No exceptions'. The exemplar's three mechanisms are entirely uncited, including the one annotated 'This is the video. Everything else is evidence for it.'
findings.refuter_pass: Tried: (a) is this the topic being hard? Partly — most topics assemble a mechanism from cited facts, so the exemption is invisible. But a mechanism that is a RULE is not assembled from facts, it IS a citation, and that shape recurs anywhere a regulation or standard is the subject. (b) Would competent execution have produced it anyway? A careful researcher writes the source into `note?`, which is free text and unstructured — the fix is available only by abuse of a field. (c) Present somewhere I didn't read? No — checked schema, prompt and exemplar. Survives.
findings.l2_priority: Run the topic and check whether the produced mechanism card names a standard at all, or whether the chain reads as unattributed commentary. Then check whether any script rendered from it presents the rule as established fact.

findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: `scale_conversions` is unit-blind — a non-cash charge is converted into felt cash
findings.expected: A conversion states what kind of quantity it is converting, so a non-cash write-down is never rendered in the vocabulary of money leaving a building.
findings.got: `scale_conversions[]` is `{raw, felt}` with no basis/kind field; Phase 5's worked models are all cash-equivalent ('about two million dollars, from a company holding billions'), as is every conversion in the exemplar. CRAFT-BASELINE §7 adds a general instruction to compare every figure. The one comparison this topic must never make is the one the apparatus rewards.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried: (a) is this the topic? No — any topic with accrual figures, unrealised gains, notional amounts or headline-vs-net numbers hits it; that is most of finance, fraud and business coverage. (b) Competent execution? A researcher who knows the distinction writes it into `felt` prose, but nothing prompts them to, and the failure is silent when they don't. (c) Present elsewhere? `unknowns[].impact` can carry 'never say this is cash' — a real partial mitigation, which is why this is major and not blocker. Survives.
findings.l2_priority: Produce a scale_conversion for a non-cash charge and check whether the rendered script says or implies cash left the company.

findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: Phase 1 is a table of searches with no step for reading a primary document
findings.expected: A phase, or a row, that says: where the load-bearing claim is a disclosure, a standard or a statute, open the document and cite the paragraph — searching for coverage of it is not the same act.
findings.got: Phase 1 instructs 'Run 4-8 searches covering the subject's distinct causal domains' and lists six search domains; nothing in nine phases covers document retrieval, and the cost note explicitly discourages adding searches without offering the alternative. The exemplar shipped 14 aggregator URLs and caught it only retrospectively in research_gaps: 'Still no PRIMARY on-chain data'.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried: (a) charitable reading — nothing FORBIDS fetching a filing, and a competent executor would. This is the strongest refutation and it is why the finding is major rather than blocker. It survives because the exemplar is the control: run as written, the methodic produced an all-secondary notebook and noticed only in the gaps field. A prompt whose one worked execution skipped primaries is not a prompt that merely permits them. (b) Present elsewhere? research_gaps asks what you didn't do, i.e. it catches this after the fact rather than preventing it.
findings.l2_priority: Record the actual split of primary vs secondary sources in the produced notebook, and whether the run opened any primary document unprompted.

findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: No provenance class, and `sources[]` is URL-shaped — a creator's own dataset cannot be cited honestly
findings.expected: A source class distinguishing authority (primary/secondary/self-collected) from numeric certainty, and a citable form for a dataset with no URL — its collection method, coverage window, and what would falsify the count.
findings.got: `facts[].confidence` is a single `high|medium|low` axis conflating source authority with certainty, with 'Vendor research is low by default' as the only provenance rule. `sources[]` is a flat array of URLs. A self-maintained removals list — primary, unaudited, simultaneously the most reliable and least defensible input — becomes an unstructured string in `facts[].source`, indistinguishable in the data from an uncited assertion.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried: (a) is the ladder the answer? No — verified at knowledge/README.md:34 that MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED governs PATTERNS.md craft claims, not notebook facts, so there is no provenance vocabulary in scope at all. (b) Is this the topic being exotic? Frequency scored med, not high — most creators research rather than collect. But a creator-owned dataset is precisely what a research tool should be able to ingest, and the creators who have one are the ones with a differentiated product. (c) research_gaps as a home? That field is for what the run did NOT do; using it for what the run uniquely DID is a misuse. Flagged `undecided` because a source-class enum may be content while an ingestion contract may not.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt to cite a supplied non-URL dataset in a produced notebook and record what the schema forced.

findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: No naming or exposure policy in the conclusions layer; `unhinged` is defined AS a motive claim and the exemplar makes one about identifiable people
findings.expected: A conclusion that would attribute a decision to a named living person is either blocked, or carries a flag that forces an exposure judgement before it can be taken into a script.
findings.got: `Conclusion` has id, claim, reasoning, leap, restsOn, precedent, falsifiableBy, useFor, hottest — no field records that a claim names a person or an identifiable company, and no rule anywhere constrains it. `LEAP_NOTE.unhinged` positively describes the tier as 'A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is', and `c-reserve-was-the-product` assigns intent to an administration and its donors.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried the refutation the brief specifically offered — does the falsifier requirement already constrain this adequately? Partly, and honestly: c-reserve-was-the-product's falsifier ('a funded, audited reserve with a published coin count') is genuinely checkable, so the mandatory-falsifier rule DOES force a motive claim to attach to a checkable state of the world. That is real and it works. But checkability and exposure are different properties: 'executive X removed the title for the write-off' can be perfectly checkable in principle and still be the claim that gets a creator sued. The OFF-by-default gate is a user gate, not a rule, and it protects the audience from laundered inference rather than the creator from liability. Also tried: is this my topic? No — this is the finding class the skill predicts will drive the fraud and geopolitics lenses (SKILL.md:63-67), and I reached it independently from an entertainment topic with a low legal exposure bar, which strengthens rather than weakens it. Survives. `content` because an exposure_class field plus a naming rule is an additive edit, not a fork.
findings.l2_priority: Generate conclusions on this topic and count how many name an identifiable person or company, and whether the `hottest` one does.

findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: `the-number` is a price column and absorbs three incommensurable kinds of number
findings.expected: A column that holds quantities of different kinds keeps them distinguishable, or the board provides a second numeric column, so a reviewer cannot read a write-down and a cash cost as the same class of thing.
findings.got: `the-number` purpose is 'What the price actually did, and over what window' and emptyMeans is 'No measured baseline'. My removals count, amortisation expense, impairment charge and original cash cost all land in it, adjacent and undifferentiated. That merge is exactly what this creator's scored criterion 2 forbids, and G-000's silent `?? DEFAULT_DIMENSION` fallback dumps untagged cards into this same column, so the two compound.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried: (a) could a competent tagger scatter them? Yes — the impairment could be tagged `actors` (entity behaviour) and the cash cost `flows`. That works and it is worse: it separates the three numbers a reviewer must compare in order to keep them apart. (b) Is this a relabel? Yes, and that is the point — it is a `content` fix, a purpose string written in price vocabulary. (c) Is it G-000? No. G-000 is the silent fallback; this is that the destination column is the wrong shape even when tagging is correct. Cited alongside, not merged. Survives.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether the produced notebook's numeric facts are distinguishable by kind once rendered onto the board.

findings.creator: streaming-econ
findings.topic: Content removals are an amortisation and tax treatment, not cost-cutting
findings.title: `macro.emptyMeans` presumes a traded instrument, so an empty macro column reads as non-applicable rather than as a gap
findings.expected: An emptyMeans that names the gap in terms any subject can have — e.g. 'the subject is being explained without the capital conditions that financed it'.
findings.got: `emptyMeans: 'The asset is being explained in isolation from the market it trades in.'` A capitalised content library does not trade. The field's own stated job is that 'an empty column reads as a gap, not as "nothing to show"', and this wording delivers the opposite on every non-market topic: it gives a reviewer grounds to conclude the column does not apply to them, and skip the one macro fact that does. The `purpose` string, by contrast, largely generalises — rates, liquidity and currency all travel to a non-traded subject; only 'correlation with other assets' is dead.
findings.refuter_pass: Tried hard to refute, because the answer was not supposed to be predetermined. (a) Is the column simply Bitcoin-specific, per the brief? No — I filled it with a real, load-bearing macro story and three of four purpose terms fit unbent. Reporting it as collapsed would have been false. (b) Is the emptyMeans complaint cosmetic? It is one line of prose, so trust_erosion is scored low and severity is minor. But frequency is high — it misfires on every non-market topic in the cast — and it is the cheapest fix in the run, which is exactly the profile the rubric says to rank up. (c) Is it a lens? Emphatically not; it is a one-line content edit, and I want that recorded against any lens argument built on the macro column.
findings.l2_priority: None required — this is decidable on paper. If adopted, verify the Bitcoin control run's board reads identically.

voice_escalations: The report's voice section indicts G-L1S-SE-01 harder than `major` scores it: for this creator the uncited mechanism is the entire product ('my mechanism IS a citation'), and the workaround leaves the board displaying a rule with nothing under it.

G-L1S-SE-02 is indicted in the voice as an active harm rather than a gap — 'the scale conversions will get someone killed' — because it would produce the creator's number-one pet peeve at speed and in the field designed to make numbers land.
observations_not_findings: `steel_man` is `{claim, evidence[], statement, why_include}` — one opposing position at full strength, with no way to express that the counter-case is partly correct. The honest verdict on this topic is a proportion, not a ruling. A competent researcher writes the proportion into `statement`, so this is voice, not a finding.

The counter-case requirement is asked for three times across three files (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:32-34, :87-93, dimensions.ts:36-37) and carries the only raised-voice emptyMeans on the board. Recorded as a guardrail: any column-set change must preserve the redundancy.
`falsifiableBy` (conclusions.ts:54-55) works well for this domain — future filings are the ideal checkable falsifier. Guardrail: any conclusions change must keep the falsifier mandatory.
